sub_scenario.one_line: release manager: rank the early window first

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the deploy plan and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The release calendar review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
The 21:00 emergency patch call last quarter went fine.
So evenings are workable?
One-off short calls are, yes.
Someone new shadowed me in the release room this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the cutover windows into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
At 06:10 this morning I went through the cutover plan line by line with coffee and caught a schema migration that clashed with the cache flush order.
Early annotation works well for you?
Best hours of my day. Quiet, sharp, no pings.
I skim overnight alerts at 06:00 daily without trouble.
So dawn reading is easy for you.
Reading, yes. That part I actually like.
I archived last cycle's notes on the release calendar and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
My evenings are locked around the daycare pickup at 17:45, and anything that runs past 17:30 gets my worst attention.
So late slots collide with the family schedule.
Every single time.
A vendor call about the deploy plan ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the release room checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the cutover windows.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the release calendar records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
Last month's 17:30 live cutover went badly: after a full day of meetings I approved the switch before the replica lag cleared, and we rolled back at 19:00.
Was that a knowledge gap?
No. I knew the checks. I was just cooked by that hour.
I sketched next week's plan for the cutover windows before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the deploy plan updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
By late afternoon my focus dips hard; my watch shows my resting heart rate climbing after 16:00 on meeting-heavy days.
A physical pattern, not a preference.
It shows up every week.
I compared two options for the release calendar tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the release room handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
The rotation form asks me to rank the 06:30 cutover window against the 17:30 one for next quarter. Which goes first, and how do I justify it?
